notes: Finding (Codex, read-only review, no statement weaker or vacuous): fn-orcs-predict-rows-at keeps every non-record row as itself. The bridge to the replay fold (books/owner-reclaim-seal.lisp fn-orcs-predict-rows-at-is-the-fold) requires fn-orcs-fold-rowsp, which excludes fn-stxa-p composites and the retained fn-held-p / fn-hstxa-p rows. A bare fn-stxa-p composite in the predictor's input is a prediction/restart mismatch (restart produces fn-hstxa-make and advances the handle; the predictor's identity loop faults it :invalid-record), but valid served reclaim input carries retained fn-hstxa-p rows, not bare composites, so no reachable live-reclaim defect is established.

Owed: a refinement through fn-rows-wire-of that relates the predicted rows of a mixed history (plain records and retained held rows) to the replay of its wire projection, contexts preserved, arena handles related. The wire-input equation without fn-orcs-fold-rowsp is false in the current implementation; composite interning, payload accounting and identity advancement would change together.

Host evidence meanwhile: tests/test_native_recovery.py test_reclaim_after_a_rotation_predicts_the_generations_a_restart_serves (article A posted under generation 1 is a retained row at the swap; its verdict generation is 1 live and after a restart).
